text:
alex: quick summary from today's host-side perf profiling: we are seeing ~3.4ms median extra per request on the host path for small prompt workloads (<=64 tokens). breakdown below, measured on canary infra (c8g-16, python worker).

maria: can you paste the profile output?

alex: pasted excerpts from pprof and flamegraph run:
```
Host CPU (sampled):
- HTTP/gRPC framing + parsing: 1.2ms
- Tokenization (sentencepiece py): 0.9ms
- JSON request parse + validation: 0.5ms
- Streaming chunking and flush path: 0.6ms
- misc (locks, logging): 0.2ms
Total ~3.4ms
```

sam: interesting that tokenization is almost 1ms — we used to be at ~0.4ms after last optimized tok caching. did something regress?

alex: yep. causality chain: recent change in request deserialization (PR #3121) switched to the new generic parser which allocates a tiny object per field; for small requests GC/alloc churn is up and tokenization lost its fast path in the py wrapper — we no longer reuse the tokenizer object across requests in the worker pool.

jin: i ran a micro-benchmark: repeated requests @1000 qps single-threaded:
- old parser + persistent tokenizer: 0.38ms tokenization
- new parser + ephemeral tokenizer: 0.92ms tokenization
So ~0.54ms extra, matches the regression.

maria: do we have perf-ci canary numbers vs prod?

perf-ci: canary baseline (7am): p50 extra host overhead 2.9ms, after deploy 3.5ms (+20%). small-prompt tail p95 worsened from 7.8ms to 10.3ms.

sam: streaming chunk path also contributes ~0.6ms. what's happening there?

alex: we flush smaller chunks more frequently after the streaming refactor; code path now does a blocking flush on each chunk boundary instead of coalescing for small writes. net effect: extra syscall+lock.

maria: suggested mitigation list:
- revert generic parser change OR patch to reuse tokenizer instance per worker (cheap). owner: alex.
- batching heuristic tweak: if requests are <128 tokens, enable micro-batching at the host parse layer to amortize JSON parse/tokenization. owner: sam.
- streaming: revert to coalesced flush or implement non-blocking buffered flush. owner: jin.
- measure gRPC vs HTTP2 framing cost — consider switching small RPCs to a lighter HTTP path. owner: infra team (cc @dev-ops).

alex: i've got a draft PR that reintroduces tokenizer pooling and pins the sentencepiece object in thread-local storage. micro-bench shows tokenization back to 0.39ms. will send for review shortly.

sam: for micro-batching i prototyped parsing N requests in one vectorized path using ujson + pre-reserved buffers. overhead per-request drops by ~0.3ms at 32x micro-batch. risks: increases tail if we wait for batch fill. we should only enable when latency SLOs allow a tiny extra queue (e.g., <=1ms max wait).

jin: streaming coalescing patch: `write_buf.append(chunk); if (buf_size > 4KB || end_of_stream) flush_async()` reduces syscalls by ~60% and p95 host overhead drops by ~1.8ms. doesn't change model runtime. PR in review.

maria: great. two follow-ups:
1) add a lightweight host-side profiler in the worker that reports per-request breakdown (tokenize/parse/flush/http) to the console so we can measure in prod. schema suggestion: 4 numbers, comma-separated. short and fast. owner: alex + perf-ci.
2) add a regression test in perf pipeline: a small-prompt scenario (<64 tokens) that fails if host overhead > 3ms p50. owner: perf-ci.

alex: creating issue for host-profiler and adding perf-ci job. also marking PR to rollback parser toyed with in #3121.

perf-ci: queued job: host-overhead-small-prompts — initial run scheduled in 15m.

sam: any plan for HTTP/gRPC path optimization? we still see ~1.2ms there.

alex: breakdown of that 1.2ms: TLS handshake negligible (keepalives used), but frame parsing + header map allocation + status code checks add ~0.9ms on average. for gRPC we do additional marshalling which costs ~0.3ms. options: enable connection pooling, reuse header maps (object pool), or move to a binary lightweight protocol for hot paths.

maria: prioritize easy wins first: tokenizer pooling (alex), streaming coalesce (jin), parser patch (alex). micro-batching and header map pooling as medium effort. longer term: evaluate switching small-hot RPCs to an optimized TCP/TLS multiplexed binary path.

alex: timeline: tokenizer PR + rollback in next 2 hrs; streaming coalesce PR merged today if no issues; perf-ci rule in place by EOD. i'll post updates here.

deploy-bot: rollout event: snapshot canary updated with rollback patch candidate at 1719001500. monitor for 30m.

maria: thanks team. ping me if perf-ci flags anything. :thumbsup:

alex: will update with before/after numbers here once canary stabilizes.

perf-ci: canary run complete: p50 host overhead now 2.6ms (improved), p95 8.1ms (improved). tokenization measured 0.41ms. streaming p95 improved 1.6ms. rolling to next stage in 10m.

sam: nice! let's still keep the micro-batching idea on the backlog.

jin: merged streaming coalesce PR to main.

alex: closing loop — pushed small doc to infra-runbook describing host profiler signals and mitigation checklist. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/host-overhead

maria: awesome work, team. small hostside wins -> meaningful product latency savings.
